title: Sprint 6 planning & design
notes: Multiple rounds of design dialog — 10 initial + 8 clarifying + 4 edge-case definition questions. Plan reshaped 3x. Final shape: B6.2 LWIN import → B6.3 schema+rules+L1 → B6.4 L2+L3+anchor+ablation → B6.5 L4+review → B6.6 execution → B6.7+ iterate → B6.N close. Tiered AI ladder with batching at L1+L2, web-grounded Sonnet at L3, Opus-inline audit at L4. Budget ceiling $250. Claude models direct via Anthropic SDK. Brand-on-label producer identity. Simple matching for LWIN import (same as prior method). 5 review upgrades + 2 safety nets + 7 gates.

title: LWIN long-tail producer import
notes: Extended pipeline/promote/lwin_long_tail.py with --resume-unlinked flag + NULL-country handling. Ran full long-tail import: 2h 51m, 24,762 producers processed (2,164 matched / 22,598 created / 0 failed), 42,566 wines + external_ids upserted, 42,566 source_lwin rows updated. Post-run discovered 26,878 rows left unlinked because wine_name was NULL/empty (main script skips those before updating source_lwin); built pipeline/promote/lwin_backfill_producer_id.py as closeout helper, backfilled all 26,878 rows via (name_normalized, country_id) lookup. Final: producers 10,683 → 33,281 (33,225 active), 0 unlinked LWIN producer_names, 26 NULL-producer_name residuals (pre-existing LWIN garbage, cannot be linked). Acceptance gate passed cleanly.

title: Pre-B6.3 hygiene: search_vector trigger fix + Opus 4.7 review
notes: User-prompted: (1) anything to revisit after Opus 4.7 1M Max upgrade? (2) is new LWIN data in same spot as existing before dedup? Q1: no plan reshape; 4 carry-forwards logged to DECISIONS.md (B6.5 review sizing upper-end, IDENTITY_RULES v1 publishable-quality, Sprint 8 bake-off judge includes 4.7, Sprint 8 L3 gate candidate); strategy-sync on open S2.9 business findings deferred to between Sprint 6 close + Sprint 7 open. Q2: audited 5 search-vector tables, found pre-existing INSERT-trigger bug on producers + wines (build_*_search_vector(NEW.id) self-query returned zero rows on BEFORE INSERT). B6.2's raw INSERTs exposed it at scale: 22,598 + 42,095 NULL search_vectors. Grapes / appellations / regions correctly inline. Migration 2026-04-16_fix_producer_wine_search_vector_trigger.sql: rewrote both functions inline (mirrors grape pattern) + backfilled NULLs via SELECT-side helper. Verified 0 NULLs, probe-INSERT populates vector, search_catalog smoke-tested. Noted for B6.3 (not fix pre-dedup): 7 NULL-country meta-entities + 5,372 zero-wine LWIN producers. Updated docs/SCHEMA.md §16 with search infra docs + patch note.

title: LWIN wine recovery via display_name + corpus-wide display_name backfill
notes: Multi-turn user push surfaced that 'zero-wine producers' were actually real wines. LWIN Guide V1.2 + source_lwin schema audit revealed a display_name column populated on 99.994% of rows (Liv-ex's authoritative combined-wine name, including Premier Cru/Grand Cru/lieu-dit info). Every LWIN-7 = real for-sale bottled product. Design: fix 26,878 skipped rows using display_name (producer prefix stripped) as wine.name; backfill wines.display_name on all LWIN-linked wines from source_lwin.display_name; REJECT rewriting wines.name on existing 162,458 (would churn slugs, invalidate caches, zero user-visible gain). Script: derive_wine_identifier() helper + --recover-missing-wines mode. Recovery run: 93.9 min, 26,616 wines created, 248 matched, 14 failed. Display_name backfill migration 2026-04-16_backfill_wines_display_name_from_lwin.sql: 100% wines.display_name coverage (all 224,316 canonical wines). Producers-with-wines: 27,842 → 33,214 (+5,372 zero-wine producers now have their village bottlings). 40 explainable residuals (pathological producer_name-includes-color + garbage wine_names + NULL-producer_name assortment cases). Meta-lesson: avoidable multi-turn back-and-forth — new CLAUDE.md Behavioral Instruction 'Check Assumptions with Web Search' logged to prevent recurrence. 3 DECISIONS.md entries.

title: Schema + IDENTITY_RULES §11 + blocking + L1 Haiku pilot + full L1 run
notes: Executed Gates 2-5 from plan. Part A: migration 2026-04-16_b6_3_producer_dedup_schema.sql extended producer_dedup_pairs with producer_id_a/_b/method_name/confidence/reasoning/cost_cents/signals/ttb_evidence/web_evidence/flag_reason/created_at/updated_at (12 new cols); unique index on (producer_id_a, producer_id_b, method_name); created producer_merge_history with RLS. Follow-up migration b6_3_producer_dedup_pairs_id_default added sequence for id column. Applied directly to production (additive, low-risk; branch reserved for B6.6 merge execution dry-run per plan). Part B: IDENTITY_RULES.md Section 11 drafted (~140 lines, 8 subsections covering MERGE/PARENT-CHILD/SKIP criteria, 12 edge cases, survivor selection, LLM-embed policy preamble, in-sprint amendment process). User reviewed 6 judgment calls; applied 1 amendment (11.4.g holdco carve-out for label-appearing brands like E. & J. Gallo). Part C: pipeline/identity/producer_blocking.py — 8 active strategies (S1 exact-norm+country=0, S2 trigram≥0.35=114,494, S5 shared-wine-LWIN=1, S6 shared-TTB-BW-permit capped 10/permit=7,595, S7 cross-country exact-OR-trigram≥0.5 OR shared LWIN=8,227, S8 shared distinguishing wines ≥30% overlap=2,018, S9 same-country substring=11,786, S10 shared rare wine name ≤5 producers=15,693, S11 cross-country word-subset=3,619). S3 embedding dropped (no producer embedding col; revisit post-L1). S4 first-3-char dropped (too permissive at 33K scale, timed out at all tuning levels). Union total: 151,150 pairs; 11,521 multi-strategy agreement (2-sig), 283 (3-sig), 64 (4-sig), 1 (5-sig). Deep-think audit surfaced 2 gaps after user pushback on US retail coverage: S10 shared-rare-wine added to catch DRC↔Romanée-Conti via 'marey monge' lieu-dit (previously 0 pairs); S11 cross-country word-subset added to catch Mondavi ↔ Mondavi & Frescobaldi. Part D: TTB spot-check on 15 random US producers confirmed BW-permit signal clean (Kenneth Volk BW-CA-7040, Emeritus BW-CA-6867, Ransom multi-state, Ridge legacy+modern BW forms). Part E: pipeline/identity/producer_dedup_l1.py built — claude-haiku-4-5 direct Anthropic, prompt caching on §11 preamble (5.4K tokens), batched 10/call, 8-worker concurrency. Pilot 200 pairs: $0.12 spent, 7/7 anchor accuracy (Ridge/Duckhorn/Caymus/DRC/Silver Oak all MERGE 0.94-0.98; Stag's Leap WC vs Stags' Leap SKIP 0.96; Silver Oak + Twomey PARENT_CHILD 0.93), 15/200 MERGE (avg conf 0.92), 21 PARENT_CHILD (0.87), 161 SKIP (0.93), 3 UNCERTAIN (0.56). User review: symmetric 0.92-0.93 threshold preferred over asymmetric, threshold decision deferred to B6.4 with full distribution. Full L1 run completed 2026-04-17 in ~5h on 8 workers, $78.32 spent (0.052¢/pair). Processed 151,120 of 151,150 pairs (99.98% — 30 batches had parse failures, acceptable). Final verdict distribution: MERGE 2,606 (1.72%, avg conf 0.88) + PARENT_CHILD 2,121 (1.40%, avg conf 0.86) + SKIP 145,310 (96.16%, avg conf 0.95) + UNCERTAIN 1,083 (0.72%, avg conf 0.56) = 4,727 total MERGE+PC candidates for ladder. Multi-strategy agreement: 139,254 @ 1-sig, 11,518 @ 2-sig, 283 @ 3-sig, 64 @ 4-sig, 1 @ 5-sig — 3+ sig pairs are overwhelmingly non-SKIP (highest-confidence auto-apply candidates). Scenario E routing preview on final distribution: L1 auto-accept ≥0.97 = 29,301 (19.4%); L1.5 Gemini cross-check 0.92-0.97 = 101,018 (66.8%); direct-to-L2 <0.92 OR UNCERTAIN = 20,801 (13.8%). Threshold discussions in-session: user rejected asymmetric thresholds ('do it right the first time'), preferred symmetric 0.92-0.93 but deferred to B6.4 calibration with L3-oracle (not user hand-labeling). Cross-model verification design adopted: L1.5 Gemini on L1 0.92-0.97 band, L2.5 Gemini on L2 0.90-0.96 band. Specific L3 routing: Gemini-aggressive + Haiku-cautious disagreements (likely FNR candidates needing web grounding). B6.4 session prompt updated with calibration-first plan: build 500-700 pair synthetic ground truth via L3 Sonnet + web_search_20250305 oracle (no user hand-labeling), run calibration analysis at each tier, pick data-driven thresholds, then full L2/L2.5/L3. Prompt caching confirmed: after initial 8 concurrent cache-writes, cache_read dominated (90% discount on 5.4K-token §11 preamble per call). L2/L3 deferred to B6.4 per plan. Sprint total $78.44 of $250, $171.56 remaining for B6.4/B6.5/B6.6/B6.7+.

title: Calibration + committed thresholds
notes: Built 600-pair stratified calibration set (T1 proxy-MERGE, T2 proxy-SKIP, T3/T4 borderline, T5 random). Gold-labeled 367 pairs: 200 proxy + 167 via Sonnet 4.6 + web_search_20250305 oracle (hit $30 cap at pair 167 of 400 hard cases). Ran L1.5 Gemini basic ($0.13, 595 pairs), L2 Haiku rich ($0.59, 600 pairs), L2.5 Gemini rich ($0.19, 600 pairs), L3 Sonnet no-web ablation ($0.65, 50 pairs). Safety Net A $0.05, 100 unblocked pairs, 0 flagged. Headline: any Haiku + any Gemini both MERGE at conf >=0.85 = 100% precision across all cross-family pairings (70-78 gold each). PC precision 6-10% uniformly across all 4 tiers (always escalate). 4-way MERGE unanimous 100% (63/63), 4-way SKIP >=0.90 96.8%, 66.2% calibration auto-handled. User committed thresholds: Stage 1 MERGE 0.88+0.88 (user chose 0.88 over calibration-supported 0.85 for safety), SKIP 0.97+0.97; Stage 2 MERGE 0.90+0.90, SKIP 0.95+0.95; Stage 3 L3 MERGE >=0.92, SKIP >=0.90. L3 web decision DEFERRED to mid-B6.5a based on residual count. SKIP audit (200 pairs) added to B6.5a to validate FN rate at scale. B6.5 split into B6.5a (automated ladder $35-80) + B6.5b (interactive review $0-5). Process changes vs original plan: L1.5 runs on ALL 151K (not just 0.92-0.97 band), L1 auto-MERGE now requires cross-family (was L1 alone >=0.97), MERGE threshold lowered from 0.97 to 0.88. Spend well under $80-95 budget (oracle 2x high per-pair, L2 calibration 70x low since only 600 pairs vs planned 30K escalation). Files: b6_4_analysis.md, final_thresholds.json+md, calibration_set.json (600 pairs), 4 per-tier calibration.md reports, crossmodel_agreement.md, agreement_matrix.md, l3_ablation.md, safety_net_a.md. Scripts: build_calibration_set.py, calibration_oracle.py, producer_dedup_gemini.py, producer_dedup_l2.py, producer_dedup_l3.py, sync_calibration.py, calibration_analysis.py, crossmodel_agreement.py, agreement_matrix.py, l3_ablation.py, safety_net_a.py, final_thresholds.py.
